newsitem.title: USA: 'Sleepers' holds onto top spot at box office.
newsitem.headline: 'Sleepers' holds onto top spot at box office.

text.p: The ensemble drama "Sleepers" enjoyed a commanding lead at the nation's box offices for the second consecutive weekend, according to studio estimates released Sunday.

The tale of revenge, whose stars include Robert De Niro, Dustin Hoffman, Brad Pitt, Jason Patric and Kevin Bacon, grossed an estimated $9.7 million during the Friday-to-Sunday period, said Warner Bros. It fell by just 21 percent from its opening weekend and has a 10-day gross of $26.48 million.
It averaged $4,678 per screen, giving it the highest ratio in the top 10. Warner Bros. is a unit of Time Warner Inc.
Elsewhere, four movies muscled their way into the top 10, and "Independence Day" passed the $300 million milestone to become the sixth-highest grossing movie in U.S. history.
The weekend's top 10 grossed an aggregate $46.3 million, up about 3 percent from the top 10 a year ago. However, most of the current crop performed weakly, as measured by their per-screen averages.
The Jon Lovitz comedy "High School High" was the highest new entry, opening at second with $7.0 million and a decent average of $3,262. The movie is released by Tristar Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp.

The horror movie "Stephen King's Thinner" scared up $5.8 million, giving it third place in its opening weekend. Released by Viacom Inc.'s Paramount Pictures, the movie averaged a humble $2,887 per screen.
Three movies vied for fourth spot, each reporting an estimated $4.4 million.

Whoopi Goldberg's latest movie, "The Associate," seemed unlikely to reverse the actress's box office freefall. The Walt Disney Co. comedy averaged just $2,471 per screen. Goldberg's recent bombs included "Bogus" and "Theodore Rex."
Paramount's fall hit "The First Wives Club" headed to a cumulative gross of $88.7 million in its sixth weekend. Its average was $1,829.

Also claiming fourth was another former number one from Paramount, "The Ghost and the Darkness." In its third week of release, the Val Kilmer-Michael Douglas African adventure has grossed $26.8 million.

Also in its third weekend, Warner Bros.' "Michael Collins" entered the top 10 at eighth with $2.5 million. The Irish historical drama had been playing in limited release on 10 screens, and this weekend widened to 738 screens.

While 20th Century Fox's "Independence Day" ranks sixth among all-time grossers with $300.7 million, it would be just 32nd if current ticket prices were applied to the estimated number of admissions to bygone hits.
According to Variety, 1939's "Gone With the Wind" would be the all-time number one with $1.25 billion. The unadjusted number one is 1982's "E.T., The Extraterrestial" with $399.8 million.
Fox is a unit of News Corp.
